answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity appear in person at a rotating checkpoint—a jetty kiosk or a meadow booth—on a random pulse each epoch. A steward matches one state-issued credential's photo to the live person, records the serial, and issues one token per slot; a serial cannot be in two places at once. Extra identities require extra people and credentials, costing C per epoch. With reward R per epoch, n sybils earn n(R-C); cloning pays only if C>R. Assumption: issuer gives one credential per person; hired impersonators or colluding stewards are the weakness.
